title: Stride-hint advisor for token-phase-aware kernel routing
creator: Marco Hernandez
description: Motivation: The runtime currently chooses kernels primarily via per-request profiles and gross sequence-length buckets. Mixed workloads with bursty short/long requests and prefill-heavy traffic show suboptimal kernel transitions during token-phase boundaries (early decode vs deep prefill), causing tail latency spikes and unnecessary cost from overprovisioned kernels. This ticket proposes a lightweight 'stride-hint' advisor: a compact estimator that tags requests with a token-phase stride fingerprint (windowed token-phase distribution + recent KV-cache hit signal) and recommends an initial kernel family and a small exploration schedule for safe online autotuning. The advisor is designed to be cheap to compute, compatible with Dedicated and Hosted routing, and to integrate with existing warmstart/warmup logic and fallback policies.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Advisor emits a kernel recommendation header for >=95% of requests within 300us overhead. 2) End-to-end p50 latency improves by >=5% and p99 does not regress vs baseline on mixed short/long synthetic workload. 3) Autotune exploration converges within 50k requests for a given customer profile and provides a documented rollback-safe fallback. 4) Telemetry surfaces per-kernel choice, stride fingerprint distribution, and regret metric in Console dashboards. 5) Unit + integration tests and a canary rollout plan exist.
technical_notes: Design: compute a stride vector over a small rolling window (e.g., last 8 requests) representing token-phase counts: prefill-heavy, decode-heavy, balanced. Combine with lightweight arch fingerprint (SM count, model variant tag) to index kernel candidates.

Heuristics: prefer kernels with lower startup overhead for decode-heavy strided profiles; prefer throughput-optimized kernels for sustained long-prefill striding. Use a tiny exploration budget (epsilon-greedy) that decays per-fingerprint to avoid oscillation.
Warmstart: read last-known best kernel for a customer+fingerprint from the runtime's kernel-store; if missing, probe 1-2 candidate microbenchmarks in background while serving on safe default kernel.
KV cache effect: include KV-hit fraction as a modifier - high KV-hit suggests decode path where small-latency kernels are preferable; low KV-hit biases toward prefill-optimized kernels.
Metrics: record selection_reason, selected_kernel_id, candidate_scores, exploration_flag, latency_tokens, and regret to enable offline analysis and automated rollbacks.

Backward compatibility: advisor exposes recommendations via an optional HTTP header; services that don't understand the header ignore it. For Private deployments, advisor can be toggled off via config.

Microbench plan: 1) microbench kernel candidates across target SM/quantization combos, 2) simulate mixed traffic traces to validate selection mapping, 3) run canary on two low-traffic customer groups.
Performance goal: keep CPU overhead <1% of request path budget by caching stride index per-connection and doing amortized updates.

Failure modes: noisy fingerprints, cold-start wrong warmstarts, exploration-induced tail noise; mitigations include smoothing, conservative epsilon decay, and immediate fallback to SLA-safe kernels on tail spikes.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): implement stride fingerprint prototype, offline mapping to candidate kernel list, and microbench harness. Owner: Aisha. ETA 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (integration): wire advisor into routing decision path, add telemetry and opt-in header, implement warmstart read/write. Owner: Aisha + Runtime infra. ETA 3 weeks.
Phase 3 (autotune): implement epsilon-greedy exploration, decay schedule, and convergence monitoring; config knobs for Dedicated and Hosted. ETA 2 weeks.
Phase 4 (canary & rollout): run canary on 2 customers, collect telemetry, tune decay and thresholds, then ramp. ETA 2 weeks.
Phase 5 (hardening): add rollback automation, dashboard drift alerts, and documentation. ETA 1 week.
Total estimate: ~10 weeks of cross-team effort with parallel microbench and infra work.
Deliverables: PRs for advisor code, microbench results, Console dashboard tile, design doc, rollout runbook.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Fingerprints too noisy -> Mitigation: apply smoothing / exponential decay, switch to per-customer aggregates when unstable.
Risk: Exploration increases p99 -> Mitigation: cap exploration during high-percentile latency windows and attach SLA-safe fallback kernel.
Risk: Additional CPU in hot path -> Mitigation: memoize per-connection stride index and evaluate offloaded background probes.
Risk: Conflicts with existing kernel warmstart store schema -> Mitigation: add versioned keys and backward-compatible read path.
Risk: Private customers requiring strict change control -> Mitigation: feature flag and config toggle; include upgrade notes in Private runbook.
tests_and_validation: Unit tests for stride computation and candidate selection heuristics; integration tests that inject mixed traces and assert selection stability; A/B canary tests comparing baseline routing to advisor-enabled routing with telemetry in Console; load-run with p99 checks. Benchmark dashboard: https://benchboards.internal.redwood/runtime/stride-advisor-2026
